newsitem.title: JAPAN: Pace of import growth to Japan slowing - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Pace of import growth to Japan slowing - MOF.

text.p: The pace of growth in imports to Japan has slowed recently, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said on Wednesday.
"Imports had shown relatively steady growth from January to March, but the pace of growth has slowed down recently," the official said.

The official was speaking to reporters after the release of trade data for the first 20 days of April, which showed Japan posted a customs-cleared trade surplus of 352.67 billion yen in the period, compared with a deficit of 59.06 billion yen in the same period a year earlier.

Free-on-board (FOB) exports in the period rose 19.9 percent from a year earlier to 2.81 trillion yen, while cost, insurance and freight (CIF) imports increased a mere 2.3 percent to 2.46 trillion yen.
The official said businesses may have increased their imports in the period up to March ahead of a tax rise in April. The consumption tax was raised to five percent from three on April 1.
A fall in crude oil prices also contributed to the decrease in import growth, he added.
As for exports, the official said car exports seem to be showing steady growth, but he did not elaborate whether it was due to the weakening of the yen. -- Tokyo Policy Desk +81-3-5473-3710
